title: Positive tensor-power sections can be compared in one invertible module
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $\mathcal L$ an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-sc-invertible-module], and $p,q\geq1$ integers. Let $s\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal L^{\otimes p})$ and $t\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal L^{\otimes q})$. For a module section $a$ write $X_a=\{x:a_x\notin\mathfrak m_x\mathcal N_x\}$, using the tensor powers and nonvanishing loci of [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]. There exist an invertible module $\mathcal M$ and $s\prime,t\prime\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal M)$ with $X_{s\prime}=X_s$ and $X_{t\prime}=X_t$. No covering, affineness or quasi-compactness hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Properties, proof of Lemma 01PY (lemma-affine-s-opens-cover-quasi-separated), second paragraph; Lemma 01PT (lemma-ample-power), proof

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor], set $\mathcal M=\mathcal L^{\otimes pq}$, which is invertible, and use the exponent-law isomorphisms to transport $s^{\otimes q}$ and $t^{\otimes p}$ into sections $s\prime,t\prime$ of $\mathcal M$.

The same lemma identifies fibre values of tensor sections with tensors of fibre values, in one-dimensional residue-field vector spaces. Choose bases: a positive power of the scalar coordinate is nonzero exactly when that scalar is nonzero. The canonical isomorphisms preserve nonzero fibre values. The nonvanishing predicate of [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module] is precisely nonzero fibre value. Hence $X_{s\prime}=X_s$ and $X_{t\prime}=X_t$.

mathlib_searches.query: Positive tensor powers of sections of an invertible sheaf have the same nonvanishing locus
mathlib_searches.results: Scheme.basicOpen_pow and RingedSpace.basicOpen_pow treat structure-sheaf sections, not sections of arbitrary invertible modules. Source grep also found compl_support_zeroLocus_tensorPowSection in WeilConjectures.AlgebraicGeometry.Modules.AffineComplement, but its locus is the complement of Hom.zeroLocus support, not nonvanishingLocus. Identifying these notions is additional work.
No hits in Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry. Separately read the source-library tensor power and zero-locus lemmas; no lemma with this nonvanishingLocus predicate.
